# PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Contents of this Part

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Title | Number

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Amendments to statements of case | Rule 17.1

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Power of court to disallow amendments made without permission | Rule 17.2

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Amendments to statements of case with the permission of the court | Rule 17.3

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE] Amendments to statements of case after the end of a relevant limitation period | Rule 17.4

## Amendments to statements of case

## 17.1

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (1) A party may amend their statement of case, including by removing, adding or substituting a party, at any time before it has been served on any other party.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (2) If his statement of case has been served, a party may amend it only –

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (a) with the written consent of all the other parties; or

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (b) with the permission of the court.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (3) If a statement of case has been served, an application to amend it by removing, adding or substituting a party must be made in accordance with rule 19.4.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (4) A party who files a notice under Part 38 discontinuing all or part of a claim may amend their statement of case without the court’s permission to give effect to the discontinuance.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.1] (Part 22 requires amendments to a statement of case to be verified by a statement of truth unless the court orders otherwise)

## Power of court to disallow amendments made without permission

## 17.2

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.2] (1) If a party has amended their statement of case where permission of the court was not required, the court may disallow the amendment.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.2] (2) A party may apply to the court for an order under paragraph (1) within 14 days of service of a copy of the amended statement of case on them.

## Amendments to statements of case with the permission of the court

## 17.3

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (1) Where the court gives permission for a party to amend their statement of case, it may give directions as to –

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (a) amendments to be made to any other statement of case; and

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (b) service of any amended statement of case.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (2) The power of the court to give permission under this rule is subject to –

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (a) rule 19.2 (change of parties – general);

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (b) rule 19.6 (special provisions about adding or substituting parties after the end of a relevant limitation period ( GL ) ); and

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.3] (c) rule 17.4 (amendments of statement of case after the end of a relevant limitation period).

## Amendments to statements of case after the end of a relevant limitation period

## 17.4

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (1) This rule applies where –

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (a) a party applies to amend their statement of case in one of the ways mentioned in this rule; and

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (b) a period of limitation has expired under –

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (i) the Limitation Act 1980 1 ;

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (ii) the Foreign Limitation Periods Act 1984 2 ; or

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (iii) any other enactment which allows such an amendment, or under which such an amendment is allowed.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (2) The court may allow an amendment whose effect will be to add or substitute a new claim, but only if the new claim arises out of the same facts or substantially the same facts as are already in issue on as a claim in respect of which the party applying for permission has already claimed a remedy in the proceedings.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (3) The court may allow an amendment to correct a mistake as to the name of a party, but only where the mistake was genuine and not one which would cause reasonable doubt as to the identity of the party in question.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (4) The court may allow an amendment to alter the capacity in which a party claims if the new capacity is one which that party had when the proceedings started or has since acquired.

[PART 17 – AMENDMENTS TO STATEMENTS OF CASE > 17.4] (Rule 19.6 specifies the circumstances in which the court may allow a new party to be added or substituted after the end of a relevant limitation period (GL) )
